summary: Registers two new DNS SRV protocol labels with IANA that are used to find instant messaging and presence services over SIP. This allows clients to locate such services through DNS.

eli5.summary: To find a chat service for a domain, you look in a directory. This note adds two entries to the list of labels so computers can locate those services.

questions: what dns srv labels are used for sip im and presence
how to find sip presence services with dns
how does an im uri resolve to a sip uri
subtitle: Registers the _sip label so im: and pres: addresses can be resolved to SIP servers through DNS.

tldr.problem: The procedures for resolving im: and pres: URIs use DNS SRV records, but no label for SIP was registered in the matching IANA registries.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers the _sip protocol label in both the Instant Messaging SRV Protocol Label registry and the Presence SRV Protocol Label registry, and shows the lookups _im._sip and _pres._sip.
tldr.outcome: Programs can now turn an address like im:fred@example.com into a SIP URI such as sip:fred@simple.example.com.

facts.label: Registries
facts.value: Instant Messaging SRV and Presence SRV

today: RFC 5509 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a SIP Label Is Needed
sections.content:
A DNS SRV record names the hosts that support a service. It is looked up in the form _Service._Proto.Name. RFC 3861 explains how to locate services for two URI schemes: im for instant inboxes and pres for presentities.

To make the link between _im, _pres and their services deterministic, IANA created two registries, one for instant messaging and one for presence. This document registers the _sip protocol label in both, so programs can resolve im: and pres: URIs down to SIP addresses.
sections.eli5: Computers look up a name to find the right server for a service. SIP was missing from the list of services they could look up.

sections.title: Resolving im: and pres: URIs
sections.content:
For instant messaging, RFC 3428 says a user agent that is given an IM URI such as im:fred@example.com SHOULD resolve it to a SIP URI. The agent does an SRV lookup for _im._sip.example.com. If the domain offers SIP instant messaging at simple.example.com, the URI resolves to sip:fred@simple.example.com.

SIP supports both pager mode and session mode instant messaging, but the SRV lookup does not say which a domain offers. A client that supports both must be ready to fall back to pager mode if session mode is rejected.

Presence works the same way, following RFC 3856. The lookup is _pres._sip.example.com, and pres:fred@example.com resolves to sip:fred@simple.example.com.
sections.eli5: You ask the phone book for the chat desk of a company, and it tells you which computer handles it.

sections.title: The IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA registers the protocol label _sip in the Instant Messaging SRV Protocol Label registry, described as the label for the use of SIP for presence and instant messaging as defined by RFC 3428. It registers the same label in the Presence SRV Protocol Label registry, with the description pointing to RFC 3856. In both cases the specification is RFC 5509.

The document does not specify a protocol, so it says there are no security issues associated with it.
sections.eli5: Two lists each get one new line saying that SIP is allowed, and this note is where it is explained.
